title: Audit sanitization can still retain or materialize large parameter payloads
reasoning: The audit entry explicitly promises bounded memory use for large parameters, but excluded keys call len(str(value)), which can materialize an entire large payload just to report its size. Non-string, non-dict, non-list values are also stored as-is, so large bytes, bytearrays, tuples, custom containers, or objects under non-excluded keys can remain in the capped deque. A capped entry count does not prevent memory exhaustion if each retained entry can contain large objects.
recommendation: Avoid stringifying excluded values for size reporting unless the value has a cheap length, and sanitize or summarize all non-scalar values instead of preserving them by reference. Treat bytes-like values and generic containers as bounded summaries, and only keep primitive scalar values directly.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests are included for audit sanitization, and the excerpted implementation contains comments for prior recursion and memory-DoS fixes without coverage evidence for bytes-like or generic object payloads.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add tests that create ToolExecutionAudit entries with very large bytes/bytearray values, excluded-key objects whose __str__ is expensive or huge, nested containers, and arbitrary objects, then assert the sanitized parameters contain bounded summaries and do not retain the original payload object.
minimumFixScope: ToolExecutionAudit._sanitize_parameters and focused backend security-policy tests.
